title: 'Drawquarium', the Aquarium for Your Drawn Fish, Confirmed for November 14 Steam Release - Inven Global
snippet:
Created by German solo developer Kaleb, Drawquarium is a single-player cozy sandbox game where players decorate an aquarium with fish and aquatic plants they draw themselves. Gameplay proceeds without competition as players cultivate an underwater world, and players can also choose preset fish instead of drawing their own. [...] # Inven Global

## 'Drawquarium', the Aquarium for Your Drawn Fish, Confirmed for November 14 Steam Release

Jaihoon    Jaihoon "Laffa" Jeong  laffa@inven.co.kr

Korean (한국어) KO   Add us on

드로우쿠아리움, 11월 14일 스팀 출시 확정

ⓒ rokaplay

rokaplay announced on the 26th that aquarium management game Drawquarium will launch on PC via Steam on November 14. Prior to release, wishlist additions have surpassed 75,000, and a new trailer announcing the release date was also revealed. [...] The demo currently distributed on Steam supports 14 languages, including Korean. rokaplay shared that user reviews for the demo were entirely positive and stated that it participated in this Steam Next Fest with a new demo featuring expanded features.

Developer Kaleb is a 3D artist working in the film industry in Berlin, Germany. Without formal education in game development, he self-taught Unreal Engine and Blueprints, creating Drawquarium as a personal passion project.

title: The Most Unexpectedly Emotional Trailer Of The Year Is For A Game About Drawing Fish - GameSpot
snippet:
Follow Us

On the one hand, the upcoming game Drawquarium looks like a sweet little cozy game. You draw fish and import them into your aquarium and your fishy friends swim around. It’s cute! But the release date trailer goes further than simply explaining the game and its features. It’s more like a short film that’s poignant and timely, and honestly, best if you just see it for yourself. [...] As the trailer suggests, the game revolves around creating your fish, housing them in your aquarium, and feeding and caring for them. You can even set your personalized aquarium as a desktop wallpaper to watch your little fishies swim around while you, let’s say, write a paper about finance. It’s a little shot of concentrated hope and humanity that put the game at the top of our cozy game radar.

Drawquarium is releasing on November 13. A demo is available now.
